'''John Michael Boardman''' (13 February 1938{{spaced ndash}}18 March 2021) was a mathematician whose speciality was [[algebraic topology|algebraic]] and [[Differential geometry and topology|differential]] topology. He was affiliated with the  [[University of Cambridge]], England and the [[Johns Hopkins University]] in [[Baltimore]], Maryland. Boardman was most widely known for his construction of the first rigorously correct model of the [[homotopy category]] of [[Spectrum (homotopy theory)|spectra]].

He received his PhD from the University of Cambridge in 1964. His thesis advisor was [[C. T. C. Wall]].<ref name=mathgene/> In 2012 he became a fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]].<ref>[https://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list List of Fellows of the American Mathematical Society], retrieved 10 November 2012.</ref> He died on 18 March 2021.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Wallach |first1=Rachel |title=Mathematician J. Michael Boardman, pioneer of the field of homotopy, dies at 83 |url=https://hub.jhu.edu/2021/03/19/michael-boardman-obituary/ |website=hub.jhu.edu |access-date=19 March 2021 |date=19 March 2021}}</ref>
